EOC Schema Cheat Sheet

AI-SUPPORTED EOC · 2026-08-12 · 491 tables (301 entries, 10 bucket groups collapsed)
    NCLOB / BLOB columns

    Several tables store large payloads in NCLOB or BLOB columns (e.g. PROCESS_DATA, CWMESSAGELOG.SEND_DATA, CWPWORKLIST.PARAMETER_JSON, EXTERNAL_OM_DATA_STORAGE.DATA). Always read as VARCHAR2 using DBMS_LOB.SUBSTR(col, 2000, 1) for NCLOB/CLOB. For BLOB: UTL_RAW.CAST_TO_VARCHAR2(DBMS_LOB.SUBSTR(col, 2000, 1)). Do not use 4000 or direct assignment — causes ORA-06502 on multibyte data.

    Core EOC Important Tables

    Jump links — each object is documented once in its category.

    • CWOPERATIONLOG JS script execution log — every run script stored in SCRIPT (NCLOB); SOURCE=`RUN JAVA SCRIPT`, OUTPUT=result/error, ISSUCCESS, ORDERID, PROCESSID, CREATED_DATE
    • CWORDERINSTANCE Order header — CWDOCID, PORTINUC, CREATIONDATE
    • CWPROCESS_NEW Process staging buckets — in CWPROCESS view; PE promotes to CWPROCESS_ACTIVE{n}
    • CWPROCESS_ACTIVE Process buckets — PROCESS_DATA NCLOB holds the process document (BPM XML, stepName)
    • CWPUSERPROC_CMD_NEW User process command poll queue — PE SELECTs ~1/sec/bucket (visible in JConsole)
    • CWPUSERPROC_CMD_ACTIVE User process command retry queue (ACTIVE) — stale orphan rows cause findProcess() storms
    • CWPWORKLIST Active human worklist / tasks
    • CWPWORKLISTARCHIVE Archived completed worklist tasks
    • CWMESSAGELOG Primary engine log (ORDER_ID, PROCESS_ID, OPERATION). SEND_DATA/RECEIVE_DATA are BLOB — read via DBMS_LOB.SUBSTR 2000
    • Views CWPROCESS, CWPACTIVITY, CWPPARTICIPANT, … (each listed once)

    ABORTED_BYCLIENTC_XJawwy — completed / closed (in use). Treat with C_C for purge and reporting

    Jawwy filters: Completed: ostate IN ('C_C','C_X'). Active provisioning: ostate IN ('O_R_PR_PONR','O_R_PRO','O_R_PRV'). Not completed: ostate NOT IN ('C_C','C_X'). Open (platform): ostate LIKE 'O_%'. Combine with CWPROCESS.STATUS when joining order → process.

    Process status (CWPROCESS.STATUS)

    CWPROCESS view / CWPROCESS_ACTIVE{n} STATUS column — numeric process state in the EOC UI.

    CodeStatus
    0Not started
    1Executing
    2Suspended
    3Completed
    4Aborted
    5Error
    6Terminated
    7Cancelled
    8Stale

    Running / stuck process queries: STATUS IN (1, 6, 7) — Executing, Terminated, Cancelled. Join to CWORDERINSTANCE on ORDER_ID = CWDOCID and filter OSTATE separately (see Order status panel above).

    Bucket number & activity index (dynamic)

    BUCKET_NO (physical table suffix 0..N-1) and ACTIVITY_INDEX are assigned dynamically per order/process at runtime — not fixed values. Bucket comes from ORDER_ID hash; activity index is the PE-assigned step instance within a process.

    BUCKET_NO (physical table suffix)

    • Never hardcode bucket numbers in generated SQL (e.g. cwprocess_active0, cwpactivity5, cwpparticipant_active12).
    • Always look up BUCKET_NO from CWPROCESS for the target ORDER_ID or PROCESS_ID before touching physical bucket tables.
    • Prefer views (CWPROCESS, CWPACTIVITY, CWPPARTICIPANT) — they UNION all buckets; no bucket suffix needed.
    • For PROCESS_DATA: SELECT bucket_no FROM cwprocess WHERE order_id = :order_id, then query cwprocess_active{bucket_no} for that row only.

    ACTIVITY_INDEX

    • Never hardcode ACTIVITY_INDEX — each running step has its own index within the process.
    • Query CWPACTIVITY view by PROCESS_ID (filter STATUS, MESSAGE_TYPE, times) to obtain ACTIVITY_INDEX.
    • When updating a physical CWPACTIVITY{n} row, n must equal CWPROCESS.BUCKET_NO for that process — derive both from lookup, never assume 0.

    Do not generate:

    • FROM cwprocess_active0 WHERE process_id = ... /* WRONG — bucket 0 is arbitrary */
    • UPDATE cwpactivity3 SET status = 1 WHERE activity_index = 2 /* WRONG — hardcoded bucket and index */
    PE NEW vs ACTIVE queues

    PE runtime uses paired *_NEW and *_ACTIVE bucket tables. NEW = incoming/staging queue (polled ~1/sec/bucket). ACTIVE = retry / delayed retry queue. JConsole on UAT shows CWPUSERPROC_CMD_NEW polls even when operational data lives in ACTIVE.

    • CWPROCESS_NEW pe Process metadata staging — in CWPROCESS view; PROCESS_DATA NCLOB when promoted
    • CWPROCESS_ACTIVE pe Active process metadata + PROCESS_DATA NCLOB (findProcess target)
    • CWPPARTICIPANT_NEW pe Incoming participant messages (poll queue)
    • CWPPARTICIPANT_ACTIVE pe Active participant messages / retries
    • CWPPARTICIPANT_GLOBAL_NEW pe Global-scope incoming participant messages
    • CWPPARTICIPANT_GLOBAL_ACTIVE pe Global-scope active participant messages
    • CWPUSERPROC_CMD_NEW pe User process command poll queue (PE polls continuously)
    • CWPUSERPROC_CMD_ACTIVE pe User process command retry queue (ACTIVE) — delete orphan rows to fix findProcess storms
    • CWPGLOBAL_NEW pe Global process command queue (single table, no bucket suffix)
    Node configuration
    • CW_NODE_CONFIG config EOC node configuration tree — hierarchical engine/feature settings per NODEID (NAME, CONFIG, PARENTID → child nodes)
    External OM Important Tables
    • EXTERNAL_OM_CONSTANTS ext Constants — defines OM constant definitions used across provisioning flows (CONSTANT_NAME, CONSTANT_VALUE, TYPE)
    • EXTERNAL_OM_DATA_STORAGE ext Temp provisioning storage — holds transient payloads while provisioning logic runs (ORDER_ID, PROCESS_ID, NAME, DATA)
    • EXTERNAL_OM_FIELD_TRANSLATION ext Translations — maps source field values to target OM representations (FIELD_NAME, SOURCE_VALUE → TARGET_VALUE)

    Cross-bucket query surfaces. Prefer these over scanning individual bucket tables. This environment has 20 buckets; production may have up to 160. BUCKET_NO and ACTIVITY_INDEX are dynamic per order/process — never hardcode bucket suffixes (e.g. cwprocess_active0) or activity indices in SQL; look up from CWPROCESS / CWPACTIVITY views first.

    Does not expose PROCESS_DATA (NCLOB). Look up BUCKET_NO here first — never hardcode cwprocess_active0; use CWPROCESS_ACTIVE{bucket_no} for that process only.    		UNION ALL of 1 identical SELECT branches (CWPROCESS_NEW0). Each branch reads one physical bucket table and projects the same metadata columns (PROCESS_ID, PARENT_ID, ROOT_ID, STATUS, BUCKET_NO, ORDER_ID, STARTTIME, etc.).     How to query CWMESSAGELOG1 queries

    Search integration message log by operation (createOrder, getOrder, ESB, Kafka) and order ID inside BLOB payloads (SEND_DATA / RECEIVE_DATA).

    CWMESSAGELOG — search by order, operation and BLOB payloadcwmessagelog_query_guide.sql

    Primary message-log query. Uncomment one OPERATION filter (e.g. om.service:omapi/createOrder). DBMS_LOB.INSTR + UTL_RAW.CAST_TO_RAW. Replace {creation_from}, {order_id}.

    46 lines
    /*
 * CWMESSAGELOG — search by order, operation, payload (BLOB)
 *
 * SEND_DATA / RECEIVE_DATA / RECEIVE_MSG_PROPS are BLOB columns.
 * Search payloads: DBMS_LOB.INSTR(col, UTL_RAW.CAST_TO_RAW('needle'), 1, 1) > 0
 * Read payload text: UTL_RAW.CAST_TO_VARCHAR2(DBMS_LOB.SUBSTR(col, 2000, 1))
 *
 * Replace {creation_from}, {order_id}. Uncomment one operation filter at a time.
 */

SELECT (b.send_time - b.receive_time) AS round_trip,
       b.msgid,
       b.order_id,
       b.process_id,
       b.operation,
       b.stepname,
       b.inter_type,
       b.creation_time,
       b.send_time,
       b.receive_time
       -- , b.*  -- full row if needed
FROM   cwmessagelog b
WHERE  b.creation_time > TO_DATE('{creation_from}', 'MM/DD/YYYY HH24:MI:SS')

-- Operation / step filters (uncomment one):
-- AND b.operation LIKE '%ECM2EAI%'
-- AND b.operation LIKE '%UPDATE_KAFKA%'
-- AND b.operation = 'om.service:omapi/createOrder'
-- AND b.operation = 'om.service:omapi/getOrder'
-- AND b.stepname LIKE '%NumberPortRequestNotification%'
-- AND b.operation = 'resourceOrder:ROM_PortType/POST_createResourceOrder'
-- AND b.operation LIKE 'jawwyIntegrationsListener.updateAPI:updateInfoAPI/UpdateOrderNotifLMD'
-- AND b.operation LIKE 'productSync.publish.ecmServices:ECM2EAI_SEND_Interface/ECM2EAI_PUBLISH_REQ'
-- AND b.operation LIKE 'ExtInterfaces.ECM.services:publishProductInESM_REST/sentDatatoESMPOST'

-- Payload search in BLOB (order ID, MSISDN, product code, etc.):
AND    DBMS_LOB.INSTR(b.send_data, UTL_RAW.CAST_TO_RAW('{order_id}'), 1, 1) > 0
-- AND DBMS_LOB.INSTR(b.receive_data, UTL_RAW.CAST_TO_RAW('{msisdn}'), 1, 1) > 0
-- AND DBMS_LOB.INSTR(b.receive_msg_props, UTL_RAW.CAST_TO_RAW('relatedEntities.type'), 1, 1) > 0
-- AND DBMS_LOB.INSTR(b.send_data, UTL_RAW.CAST_TO_RAW('BTL_PKG_PERCENTAGE_DISCOUNT'), 800, 1) > 0

-- Slow round-trip only (> 1 second):
-- AND (b.send_time - b.receive_time) > NUMTODSINTERVAL(1, 'SECOND')

ORDER  BY b.creation_time DESC;
    Sizing and volume4 queries

    Row counts and monthly rollups for capacity planning (CWPROCESS, CWORDERINSTANCE).

    CWPROCESS — unique orders per month by process STATUScwprocess_active_orders_by_date.sql

    Each ORDER_ID once; month = earliest STARTTIME. STATUS labels match EOC UI (0–8).

    WITH proc AS (
    SELECT p.order_id, p.process_id, p.starttime, p.status
    FROM   cwprocess p
    WHERE  p.order_id IS NOT NULL
),
order_one AS (
    SELECT order_id,
           TRUNC(first_starttime, 'MM') AS run_month,
           process_count,
           order_status
    FROM (
        SELECT p.order_id,
               MIN(p.starttime) OVER (PARTITION BY p.order_id) AS first_starttime,
               COUNT(*)       OVER (PARTITION BY p.order_id) AS process_count,
               FIRST_VALUE(p.status) OVER (
                   PARTITION BY p.order_id
                   ORDER BY p.starttime, p.process_id
               ) AS order_status,
               ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
                   PARTITION BY p.order_id
                   ORDER BY p.starttime, p.process_id
               ) AS rn
        FROM   proc p
    )
    WHERE  rn = 1
)
SELECT TO_CHAR(o.run_month, 'YYYY-MM') AS run_month,
       o.order_status AS status,
       DECODE(o.order_status,
           0, 'Not started', 1, 'Executing', 2, 'Suspended', 3, 'Completed',
           4, 'Aborted', 5, 'Error', 6, 'Terminated', 7, 'Cancelled',
           8, 'Stale', 'Unknown') AS status_label,
       SUM(o.process_count) AS process_count,
       COUNT(*)             AS unique_order_count
FROM   order_one o
GROUP  BY o.run_month, o.order_status
ORDER  BY o.run_month DESC, o.order_status

    Deploy & run get_stuck_orders_with_current_stepget_stuck_orders_deploy_and_run.sql

    Self-contained: extract_step_name, get_active_process_union_sql, get_stuck_orders_with_current_step + ref cursor. SQL Developer: Ctrl+A → F5. Edit date window in section 4.

    150 lines
    /*
 * Stuck orders — full deploy + run (self-contained)
 *
 * Creates:
 *   1. extract_step_name          — read <stepName> from PROCESS_DATA NCLOB
 *   2. get_active_process_union_sql — UNION ALL over CWPROCESS_ACTIVE*
 *   3. get_stuck_orders_with_current_step — ref cursor report
 *
 * SQL Developer: Ctrl+A then F5 (Run Script), NOT F9
 * Edit dates in section 4 before running.
 */

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1) Extract <stepName> from PROCESS_DATA
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION extract_step_name(p_process_data IN CLOB)
RETURN VARCHAR2
IS
  v_data      VARCHAR2(32767);
  v_open_tag  VARCHAR2(20) := CHR(60) || 'stepName' || CHR(62);
  v_close_tag VARCHAR2(21) := CHR(60) || '/stepName' || CHR(62);
  v_start     NUMBER;
  v_end       NUMBER;
  v_len       NUMBER;
BEGIN
  IF p_process_data IS NULL THEN RETURN NULL; END IF;
  v_len := DBMS_LOB.getlength(p_process_data);
  IF v_len = 0 THEN RETURN NULL; END IF;
  v_data := DBMS_LOB.SUBSTR(p_process_data, LEAST(v_len, 32767), 1);
  v_start := INSTR(v_data, v_open_tag);
  IF v_start = 0 THEN RETURN NULL; END IF;
  v_start := v_start + LENGTH(v_open_tag);
  v_end   := INSTR(v_data, v_close_tag, v_start);
  IF v_end = 0 OR v_end <= v_start THEN RETURN NULL; END IF;
  RETURN SUBSTR(v_data, v_start, v_end - v_start);
EXCEPTION
  WHEN OTHERS THEN RETURN NULL;
END extract_step_name;
/


-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2) Build UNION ALL over CWPROCESS_ACTIVE* tables
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION get_active_process_union_sql
RETURN VARCHAR2
IS
  c_prefix     CONSTANT VARCHAR2(30) := 'CWPROCESS_ACTIVE';
  v_union_sql  VARCHAR2(32767) := NULL;
  v_bucket_num NUMBER;
BEGIN
  FOR t IN (
    SELECT ut.table_name
      FROM user_tables ut
     WHERE UPPER(ut.table_name) LIKE c_prefix || '%'
     ORDER BY ut.table_name
  ) LOOP
    v_bucket_num := TO_NUMBER(SUBSTR(UPPER(t.table_name), LENGTH(c_prefix) + 1));
    IF v_union_sql IS NOT NULL THEN
      v_union_sql := v_union_sql || ' UNION ALL ';
    END IF;
    v_union_sql := v_union_sql
      || 'SELECT ' || v_bucket_num || ' AS bucket_num, a.process_id, a.process_data '
      || 'FROM ' || t.table_name || ' a';
  END LOOP;

  IF v_union_sql IS NULL THEN
    RAISE_APPLICATION_ERROR(-20001, 'No CWPROCESS_ACTIVE* tables found.');
  END IF;

  RETURN v_union_sql;
END get_active_process_union_sql;
/


-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3) Ref cursor procedure
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE get_stuck_orders_with_current_step (
  p_date_from   IN  DATE,
  p_date_to     IN  DATE,
  p_result      OUT SYS_REFCURSOR
)
IS
  v_union_sql  VARCHAR2(32767);
  v_final_sql  VARCHAR2(32767);
BEGIN
  v_union_sql := get_active_process_union_sql();

  v_final_sql :=
    'SELECT '
  || '  o.CWDOCID, '
  || '  o.OSTATE, '
  || '  LISTAGG(p.PROCESS_ID, '', '') '
  || '    WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY p.PROCESS_ID) AS PROCESS_IDS, '
  || '  MAX(p.LAST_USED_DATE) AS LAST_USED_DATE, '
  || '  LISTAGG(DISTINCT TO_CHAR(p.STATUS), '', '') '
  || '    WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY TO_CHAR(p.STATUS)) AS STATUSES, '
  || '  ml.STEP_NAMES, '
  || '  pcs.CURRENT_STEPNAMES, '
  || '  LISTAGG(DISTINCT TO_CHAR(p.BUCKET_NO), '', '') '
  || '    WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY p.BUCKET_NO) AS PROCESS_BUCKETS '
  || 'FROM CWORDERINSTANCE o '
  || 'JOIN CWPROCESS p ON p.ORDER_ID = o.CWDOCID '
  || 'LEFT JOIN ( '
  || '  SELECT ml_inner.ORDER_ID, '
  || '         LISTAGG(ml_inner.STEPNAME, '', '' ON OVERFLOW TRUNCATE ''...'' WITHOUT COUNT) '
  || '           WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ml_inner.CREATION_TIME) AS STEP_NAMES '
  || '    FROM CWMESSAGELOG ml_inner '
  || '   WHERE ml_inner.STEPNAME <> ''UPDATE_ORDER_SATATE_ERROR'' '
  || '     AND ml_inner.STEPNAME IS NOT NULL '
  || '   GROUP BY ml_inner.ORDER_ID '
  || ') ml ON ml.ORDER_ID = o.CWDOCID '
  || 'LEFT JOIN ( '
  || '  SELECT p2.ORDER_ID, '
  || '         LISTAGG(DISTINCT extract_step_name(a.process_data), '', '' ON OVERFLOW TRUNCATE ''...'' WITHOUT COUNT) '
  || '           WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY extract_step_name(a.process_data)) AS CURRENT_STEPNAMES '
  || '    FROM CWPROCESS p2 '
  || '    JOIN (' || v_union_sql || ') a '
  || '      ON a.process_id = p2.PROCESS_ID AND a.bucket_num = p2.BUCKET_NO '
  || '   WHERE p2.STATUS IN (''1'',''3'',''6'',''7'') '
  || '     AND extract_step_name(a.process_data) IS NOT NULL '
  || '   GROUP BY p2.ORDER_ID '
  || ') pcs ON pcs.ORDER_ID = o.CWDOCID '
  || 'WHERE p.STATUS IN (''1'',''3'',''6'',''7'') '
  || '  AND o.CREATIONDATE >= :p_date_from '
  || '  AND o.CREATIONDATE <  :p_date_to '
  || 'GROUP BY o.CWDOCID, o.OSTATE, ml.STEP_NAMES, pcs.CURRENT_STEPNAMES';

  OPEN p_result FOR v_final_sql USING p_date_from, p_date_to;
END get_stuck_orders_with_current_step;
/


-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 4) Run report — edit date range, then F5 entire script
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
VAR rc REFCURSOR

BEGIN
  get_stuck_orders_with_current_step(
    TO_DATE('07/30/2026 00:00:00', 'MM/DD/YYYY HH24:MI:SS'),
    TO_DATE('07/30/2026 23:59:59', 'MM/DD/YYYY HH24:MI:SS'),
    :rc
  );
END;
/

PRINT rc
    Running orders — inline SELECT with last message stepget_orders_with_current_step.sql

    CWPROCESS STATUS IN (1, 6, 7): Executing, Terminated, Cancelled. Does not read stepName from PROCESS_DATA NCLOB.

    SELECT o.cwdocid, o.ostate,
       LISTAGG(p.process_id, ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY p.process_id) AS process_ids,
       MAX(p.last_used_date) AS last_used_date,
       ml.stepname AS last_msg_step
FROM   cworderinstance o
JOIN   cwprocess p ON p.order_id = o.cwdocid
LEFT   JOIN (
    SELECT order_id, stepname,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY creation_time DESC) AS rn
    FROM   cwmessagelog
    WHERE  stepname IS NOT NULL
      AND  stepname <> 'UPDATE_ORDER_SATATE_ERROR'
) ml ON ml.order_id = o.cwdocid AND ml.rn = 1
WHERE  p.status IN ('1', '6', '7')
  AND  o.ostate NOT IN ('C_C', 'C_X')
  AND  o.creationdate >= TO_DATE('2026-07-01', 'YYYY-MM-DD')
  AND  o.creationdate <  TO_DATE('2026-08-01', 'YYYY-MM-DD')
GROUP  BY o.cwdocid, o.ostate, ml.stepname
ORDER  BY last_used_date

    CWMESSAGELOG step monitoring2 queries

    Integration step latency and last-step position for running orders. Joins CWORDERINSTANCE + CWMESSAGELOG on ORDER_ID / USER_DATA1.

    Step latency rollup by operation / stepnamecwmessagelog_step_latency.sql

    Edit creation_from in params CTE. stuck_count = sent, no receive. PERCENTILE_CONT p95 round-trip seconds.

    WITH params AS (
    SELECT TIMESTAMP '2026-07-01 00:00:00' AS creation_from FROM dual
),
logs AS (
    SELECT ml.msgid, ml.creation_time, ml.inter_type,
           ml.order_id AS order_id, ml.operation,
           NVL(NULLIF(TRIM(ml.stepname), ''), '(no stepname)') AS stepname,
           ml.send_time, ml.receive_time
    FROM   cworderinstance o
    CROSS  JOIN params p
    JOIN   cwmessagelog ml ON ml.order_id = o.cwdocid
    WHERE  o.creationdate >= CAST(p.creation_from AS DATE)
    UNION ALL
    SELECT ml.msgid, ml.creation_time, ml.inter_type,
           ml.user_data1 AS order_id, ml.operation,
           NVL(NULLIF(TRIM(ml.stepname), ''), '(no stepname)') AS stepname,
           ml.send_time, ml.receive_time
    FROM   cworderinstance o
    CROSS  JOIN params p
    JOIN   cwmessagelog ml ON ml.user_data1 = o.cwdocid
    WHERE  o.creationdate >= CAST(p.creation_from AS DATE)
      AND  ml.order_id IS NULL
      AND  ml.user_data1 IS NOT NULL
),
step_stats AS (
    SELECT operation, stepname,
           COUNT(*) AS calls,
           SUM(CASE
               WHEN receive_time IS NULL AND inter_type <> 0
                AND operation NOT LIKE 'KAFKAEVENT_%' AND send_time IS NOT NULL
               THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS stuck_count,
           SUM(CASE
               WHEN inter_type = 0 OR operation LIKE 'KAFKAEVENT_%'
               THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS event_count,
           ROUND(AVG(CASE
               WHEN send_time IS NOT NULL AND receive_time IS NOT NULL
                AND receive_time >= send_time
               THEN EXTRACT(DAY    FROM (receive_time - send_time)) * 86400
                  + EXTRACT(HOUR   FROM (receive_time - send_time)) * 3600
                  + EXTRACT(MINUTE FROM (receive_time - send_time)) * 60
                  + EXTRACT(SECOND FROM (receive_time - send_time))
           END), 1) AS avg_sec,
           ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY CASE
               WHEN send_time IS NOT NULL AND receive_time IS NOT NULL
                AND receive_time >= send_time
               THEN EXTRACT(DAY    FROM (receive_time - send_time)) * 86400
                  + EXTRACT(HOUR   FROM (receive_time - send_time)) * 3600
                  + EXTRACT(MINUTE FROM (receive_time - send_time)) * 60
                  + EXTRACT(SECOND FROM (receive_time - send_time))
           END), 1) AS p95_sec
    FROM logs
    GROUP BY operation, stepname
),
order_last AS (
    SELECT order_id, operation, stepname, inter_type, send_time, receive_time
    FROM (
        SELECT l.*,
               ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
                   PARTITION BY order_id
                   ORDER BY creation_time DESC, msgid DESC
               ) AS rn
        FROM logs l
    )
    WHERE rn = 1
),
last_stats AS (
    SELECT operation, stepname,
           COUNT(*) AS last_step,
           SUM(CASE
               WHEN receive_time IS NULL AND inter_type <> 0
                AND operation NOT LIKE 'KAFKAEVENT_%' AND send_time IS NOT NULL
               THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS last_step_stuck
    FROM order_last
    GROUP BY operation, stepname
)
SELECT s.operation, s.stepname, s.calls, s.stuck_count, s.event_count,
       NVL(l.last_step, 0) AS last_step,
       NVL(l.last_step_stuck, 0) AS last_step_stuck,
       s.avg_sec, s.p95_sec
FROM   step_stats s
LEFT   JOIN last_stats l
       ON l.operation = s.operation AND l.stepname = s.stepname
ORDER  BY s.stuck_count DESC, last_step_stuck DESC, s.calls DESC
    Last CWMESSAGELOG step per running orderad-hoc

    Running processes only: CWPROCESS STATUS IN (1, 6, 7). Lightweight view when full latency rollup is not needed.

    SELECT o.cwdocid, o.ostate, p.process_id, p.status AS process_status,
       p.last_used_date, ml.stepname AS last_integration_step
FROM   cworderinstance o
JOIN   cwprocess p ON p.order_id = o.cwdocid
LEFT   JOIN (
    SELECT order_id, stepname,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY creation_time DESC) AS rn
    FROM   cwmessagelog
    WHERE  stepname IS NOT NULL
      AND  stepname <> 'UPDATE_ORDER_SATATE_ERROR'
) ml ON ml.order_id = o.cwdocid AND ml.rn = 1
WHERE  p.status IN ('1', '6', '7')
  AND  o.ostate NOT IN ('C_C', 'C_X')
  AND  o.creationdate >= TIMESTAMP '2026-07-01 00:00:00'

    Orphan row previews5 queries

    COUNT queries before bucket DELETE scripts. Orphan PE rows (especially CWPUSERPROC_CMD_ACTIVE) cause findProcess() storms.

    CWPROCESS_ACTIVE — process with no CWORDERINSTANCEorphan_processes.sql

    Template bucket 0; repeat for cwprocess_active1..N.

    SELECT COUNT(*) AS orphan_processes
FROM   cwprocess_active0 p
WHERE  NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM cworderinstance o WHERE o.cwdocid = p.order_id
)
    CWPPARTICIPANT_ACTIVE — participant with no CWPROCESSorphan_cwpparticipant_active.sql

    Template bucket 0; repeat per bucket.

    SELECT COUNT(*) AS orphan_participants
FROM   cwpparticipant_active0 t
WHERE  NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM cwprocess p WHERE p.order_id = t.order_id
)
    CWPPARTICIPANT_GLOBAL — ORDER_ID with no processorphan_cwpparticipant_global.sql

    Only ORDER_ID IS NOT NULL (skips order-less MNP notifications).

    SELECT COUNT(*) AS orphan_global
FROM   cwpparticipant_global_new0 t
WHERE  t.order_id IS NOT NULL
  AND  NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM cwprocess p WHERE p.order_id = t.order_id
)
    CWPUSERPROC_CMD_ACTIVE — orphan PROCESS_ID (findProcess storm)ad-hoc

    PROCESS_ID with no CWPROCESS match — PE retry loop risk. Template bucket 0.

    SELECT COUNT(*) AS orphan_cmd_rows
FROM   cwpuserproc_cmd_active0 c
WHERE  NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM cwprocess p WHERE p.process_id = c.process_id
)
    CWMESSAGELOG — rows with no process or orderorphan_process_reference_queries_final.sql

    Full DELETE patterns in orphan_process_reference_queries_final_v3.sql.

    SELECT COUNT(*) AS orphan_msglog_rows
FROM   cwmessagelog t
WHERE  NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM cwprocess p
    WHERE p.process_id = t.process_id OR p.order_id = t.order_id
)
    28 patterns · 7 categories

    Production workaround patterns for stuck processes, External OM, MNP port-in, and backend activity fixes. Replace placeholders. PROD only — preview first.

    Complete reference scripts3 patterns

    Downloadable SQL/JS templates covering all patterns below.

    Compiled PROD workaround script (PS, External OM, orders)

    When: Starting point — stuck PS, External OM, order flags, diagnostics.

    PROD only. Replace placeholders. SELECT previews first; COMMIT per step.

    161 lines
    /*
 * PROD workarounds — core patterns (stuck PS, orders, External OM, diagnostics)
 *
 * WARNING: PROD-only manual fixes. Always:
 *   - Identify PROCESS_ID, BUCKET_NO (CWPROCESS), ACTIVITY_INDEX before updates
 *   - Run SELECT previews first; COMMIT each step
 *   - Many WAs require Suspend PS → Resume PS from EOC UI after SQL steps
 * Replace {bucket}, {process_id}, {activity_index}, {order_id}, {msisdn} before run.
 */

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 0) Lookup helpers (run first)
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Bucket for process → CWPROCESS_ACTIVE{bucket}
SELECT process_id, order_id, status, bucket_no, last_used_date
FROM   cwprocess
WHERE  process_id = '{process_id}';

-- Stuck activity index
SELECT process_id, activity_index, status, repeat_count, start_time, completion_time, message_type
FROM   cwpactivity{bucket}
WHERE  process_id = '{process_id}'
ORDER  BY activity_index;

-- Message log tail for order
SELECT order_id, stepname, operation, creation_time, inter_type
FROM   cwmessagelog
WHERE  order_id = '{order_id}'
ORDER  BY creation_time DESC
FETCH FIRST 30 ROWS ONLY;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1) Standard stuck-PS workaround (most common War Room pattern)
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Step 1: remove activities after stuck index
DELETE FROM cwpactivity{bucket}
WHERE  process_id = '{process_id}'
  AND  activity_index > {activity_index};
COMMIT;

-- Step 2: set stuck activity to running (status 1)
UPDATE cwpactivity{bucket}
SET    status = '1'
WHERE  process_id = '{process_id}'
  AND  activity_index = {activity_index};
COMMIT;

-- Step 3: Suspend PS from EOC UI
-- Step 4: Resume PS from EOC UI

-- Optional — if process is suspended (status 6/7):
UPDATE cwprocess_active{bucket}
SET    status = '1'
WHERE  process_id = '{process_id}';
COMMIT;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2) Activity retry storm — REPEAT_COUNT stuck at 59
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
UPDATE cwpactivity{bucket}
SET    repeat_count = '0'
WHERE  process_id = '{process_id}'
  AND  repeat_count = '59';
COMMIT;

-- Variant with activity_index (some tickets):
UPDATE cwpactivity{bucket}
SET    repeat_count = '0'
WHERE  process_id = '{process_id}'
  AND  activity_index = {activity_index};
COMMIT;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3) Order cancellation flag — unblock cancel flow
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
UPDATE cworderinstance
SET    iscancellation = '0'
WHERE  cwdocid = '{order_id}';
COMMIT;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 4) External OM — investigation queries
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
SELECT * FROM external_om_order_status WHERE order_status = 'PENDING';

SELECT * FROM external_om_order_mapping WHERE om_order_id = '{order_id}';

SELECT * FROM external_om_constants WHERE request_id = 'ICCID_PATCH';

SELECT msg_id, order_id, process_id, name, created_on
FROM   external_om_data_storage
WHERE  order_id = '{order_id}'
ORDER  BY created_on DESC;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 5) CWT_DO_RELATEDOBJECTS — delete corrupted Account row
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
DELETE FROM cwt_do_relatedobjects
WHERE  orderid IN ({order_id_list})
  AND  name = 'Account'
  AND  value = '{account_value}';
COMMIT;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 6) Agent ID missing on offline orders (ESB_029_ManageStock WA)
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
SELECT ro1.orderid AS order_id, ro1.value AS agent_id, ro1.createdon AS creation_time
FROM   cwt_do_relatedobjects ro1
JOIN   cwt_do_relatedobjects ro2 ON ro1.orderid = ro2.orderid
JOIN   cwt_do_relatedobjects ro3 ON ro1.orderid = ro3.orderid
WHERE  ro1.name = 'Agent'
  AND  ro1.value IS NOT NULL
  AND  ro1.orderid IN (
    SELECT cwdocid FROM cworderinstance
    WHERE (newactivationuc = 1 OR simswapuc = 1 OR portinuc = 1)
      AND ostate = 'C_C'
  )
  AND  ro2.name = 'triggeringSystem'
  AND  ro2.value = 'OFFLINE'
  AND  ro3.name = 'Agent'
  AND  ro3.value IS NULL
ORDER  BY ro1.createdon DESC;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 7) In-progress orders for subscriber (corrupted order blocking new orders)
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
SELECT cwdocid, ostate, creationdate
FROM   cworderinstance
WHERE  ostate NOT IN ('C_C', 'C_X')
  AND  cwdocid IN (
    SELECT orderid FROM cwt_do_relatedobjects
    WHERE name = 'Subscriber' AND value = '{msisdn}'
  )
ORDER  BY creationdate DESC;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 8) CWOPERATIONLOG — JS script execution trace
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
SELECT *
FROM   cwoperationlog
WHERE  orderid = '{order_id}'
ORDER  BY created_date DESC;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 9) Orders without Mobile Line PO (sizing — ticket 11008208)
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
SELECT DISTINCT oi.cwdocid
FROM   cworderinstance oi
JOIN   cwpc_basket b ON b.cworderid = oi.cwdocid
WHERE  NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM cwpc_basketitem bi
    WHERE bi.basketid = b.basketid
      AND bi.itemcode = 'PS_MOBILE_LINE'
);

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 10) Explain plan (DBA — slow CWPROCESS_ACTIVE parent lookup)
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
SELECT * FROM TABLE(DBMS_XPLAN.DISPLAY_CURSOR(NULL, NULL, 'ALLSTATS LAST'));

    Backend activity manipulation script

    When: Direct CWPACTIVITY DELETE/INSERT plus Process.resumeProcess.

    For corrupt or missing activity rows when UI resume is insufficient.

    93 lines
    /*
 * PROD workarounds — backend CWPACTIVITY manipulation
 *
 * Backend process-activity manipulation:
 *   1) DELETE activity index range
 *   2) INSERT replacement activity row
 *   3) Process.resumeProcess(PS) in EOC JS console
 *   4) Process.resumeProcess(UC) in EOC JS console
 *
 * Replace {bucket}, {process_id}, {uc_process_id}, index/time placeholders.
 * PROD only — SELECT activities first, COMMIT per step.
 */

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 0) Lookup — bucket & current activities (run first)
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
SELECT process_id, order_id, status, bucket_no
FROM   cwprocess
WHERE  process_id IN ('{process_id}', '{uc_process_id}');

SELECT activity_index, status, repeat_count, start_time, completion_time
FROM   cwpactivity{bucket}
WHERE  process_id = '{process_id}'
ORDER  BY activity_index;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1) Delete stuck / bad activity range
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
DELETE FROM cwpactivity{bucket}
WHERE  process_id = '{process_id}'
  AND  activity_index >= {activity_index_from}
  AND  activity_index <= {activity_index_to};
COMMIT;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2) Insert replacement activity (STATUS 1 = Executing)
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
INSERT INTO cwpactivity{bucket} (
    process_id, activity_index, long_data_id, long_data_id_sent,
    start_time, start_time_ms, completion_time, end_time_ms,
    status, parallel_count, repeat_count, message_type
)
VALUES (
    '{process_id}', {new_activity_index}, 0, 0,
    TO_DATE('{start_time}', 'MM/DD/YYYY HH24:MI:SS'), 0,
    NULL, 0, 1, 0, 0, NULL
);
COMMIT;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3) Resume PS process — EOC JS console
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
/*
var processID = "{process_id}";
Process.resumeProcess(processID);
processID;
*/

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 4) Resume UC (parent) process — EOC JS console
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
/*
var processID = "{uc_process_id}";
Process.resumeProcess(processID);
processID;
*/

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Variant — INSERT only (no range delete) — simpler stuck-step recovery
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
INSERT INTO cwpactivity{bucket} (
    process_id, activity_index, long_data_id, long_data_id_sent,
    start_time, start_time_ms, completion_time, end_time_ms,
    status, parallel_count, repeat_count, message_type
)
VALUES (
    '{process_id}', {new_activity_index}, 0, -1,
    NULL, 0, NULL, 0, 1, 0, 0, NULL
);
COMMIT;

-- Then Process.resumeProcess('{process_id}');

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Optional — force suspend before resume cycle (some MNP / stuck PS tickets)
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
UPDATE cwprocess_active{bucket}
SET    status = '2'
WHERE  process_id = '{process_id}';
COMMIT;

-- Then steps 3–4 (Process.resumeProcess) or UI Suspend → Resume

    Stuck process recovery6 patterns

    Unblock frozen PS/process steps. Most patterns end with Suspend → Resume PS from EOC UI, or Process.resumeProcess in JS console.

    Trim future activities & restart stuck step (most common)

    When: PS frozen mid-flow — process alive but step will not advance. Delete activities after the stuck ACTIVITY_INDEX, set current step to Executing (1).

    1) DELETE activities with index > stuck 2) UPDATE stuck activity STATUS=1 3) Suspend PS in UI 4) Resume PS in UI. Optional: CWPROCESS_ACTIVE STATUS=1 if suspended.

    DELETE FROM cwpactivity{bucket}
WHERE  process_id = '{process_id}'
  AND  activity_index > {activity_index};
COMMIT;

UPDATE cwpactivity{bucket}
SET    status = '1'
WHERE  process_id = '{process_id}'
  AND  activity_index = {activity_index};
COMMIT;

-- Suspend PS from EOC UI, then Resume PS from EOC UI

UPDATE cwprocess_active{bucket}
SET    status = '1'
WHERE  process_id = '{process_id}';
COMMIT;
    Break activity retry loop (REPEAT_COUNT stuck at 59)

    When: Single step retrying until max attempts — engine hammers same activity.

    Reset REPEAT_COUNT to 0, then Suspend/Resume PS from UI.

    UPDATE cwpactivity{bucket}
SET    repeat_count = '0'
WHERE  process_id = '{process_id}'
  AND  repeat_count = '59';
COMMIT;

-- Or target a specific step:
UPDATE cwpactivity{bucket}
SET    repeat_count = '0'
WHERE  process_id = '{process_id}'
  AND  activity_index = {activity_index};
COMMIT;
